input.brief: LIMOVI: one Gold Balance that turns Indian household gold into jewellery experiences, loans, liquidity, dividends and gifts

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Anchored text, specimen half
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split exactly in half by two flat tones that meet at a clean vertical edge: the ground on the left, a palette colour on the right. Left half: the wordmark sits top-left on a 40px margin; the next two thirds of the height are empty; everything else is anchored bottom-left and ends 40px above the bottom edge: a headline on one or two lines at clamp(28px, 2.6vw, 40px), medium weight; one sentence at 18px in the soft ink, max 38ch; the single action as a solid rectangle. Right half: position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh. In its centre sits a square tile in a second palette colour, 450px wide (31vw) with a 24px radius, holding one cut-out item at 70% of the tile, object-fit: contain, mix-blend-mode: multiply on light fills. Under the tile's left corner the item's name and one fact sit at 15px. As the left column scrolls through the catalogue, the tile's item and colour swap to match the entry in view. One text link sits top-right on the colour field.
hero.mobile: The colour half comes first as a block 52svh tall holding the square tile at 62vw, centred, and stays sticky while the text slides over its lower edge. The text block follows on the ground: the headline at 7vw on two lines, the sentence at 16px, the action full width. The wordmark and one link sit on the top row over the colour.
hero.headline: A modest 3-6 word line at 28-40px, at most 40 characters; the object, not the type, carries the screen.

type.note: A wide display sans built from rounded squares, heavy and a little architectural, beside a clean text grotesk. Suits architecture indexes, watches, mobility and events that want a title with a constructed feel.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Heading captions a panorama
sections.blueprint: The section is exactly 100svh. Its top third holds a two-line heading of three to six words at clamp(48px, 6.5vw, 96px) with leading 0.95, either centred or flush left on the page margin. 28px beneath the heading sit two small captions side by side, each two lines at 13px and 150px wide with a 48px gap, aligned to the heading (centred as a pair, or both starting at its left edge). 40px below them a full-bleed photograph begins and runs off the bottom of the viewport: it is 100vw wide at 21:9 or wider, and only its top 55–60svh is visible before the fold, the rest arriving with scroll. The heading therefore reads as a large caption to the picture. On an object-led page the image is the object on a flat dark panel inset by the page margin instead of bleeding to the edges.
sections.mobile: Heading at 12vw on two lines, left-aligned, taking the top 30% of the screen. The two captions merge into one four-line block at 14px. The photograph begins at 45% of the screen height in a 4:5 crop, full-bleed, and runs off the bottom.

sections.name: Capabilities at poster scale
sections.blueprint: No images. The heading, two to four words, is the first line of the list itself, set at the same size as the items but in the soft ink, so no separate title sits above. Five to eight capability names follow, one per line, at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 84px), medium to heavy weight, leading 1.0, tight tracking, flush left on the page margin across columns 1–8 of 12. Each name's one-sentence description is set at 16–18px in columns 9–12, its first baseline aligned with the name's baseline (CSS grid, align-items: first baseline). Rows are separated by 0.35em of space and nothing else. On hover one row keeps full ink while the others fall to 35% opacity. Leave 18–22vh of empty ground above and below; nothing else shares the section.
sections.mobile: Names drop to 11vw and stay one per line; a name that will not fit breaks onto a second line with a hanging indent. Each description sits directly under its name at 16px, indented one margin width, with 28px before the next name. The soft-ink heading line stays as the first row. All rows at full ink.

sections.name: Object in front of type
sections.blueprint: Type and object share one space instead of sitting side by side. Three or four lines of display type, one or two words each, are stacked flush left at clamp(72px, 9vw, 150px) with leading 0.88, starting on the left margin and allowed to leave the right edge (white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden on the section). The lines step through tones of one ink: one at 45%, one at full strength, the rest at 18%. The object photograph, a cut-out or a studio shot blended with multiply, is absolutely positioned over the upper right of the stack at 40–46vw wide, rotated no more than 6 degrees and above the type in the stacking order, so it hides parts of three or four letters. Under the stack, in columns 8–12, a two-paragraph block at 20px gives the facts. The full-strength line is the heading; nothing sits above it.
sections.mobile: Type drops to 15vw and still runs off the right edge. The object sits at 78vw wide, overlapping the last two lines from below instead of from the right, and is cropped by the right edge. The facts block follows at full width and 17px.

sections.name: Tiles that grow
sections.blueprint: Order is carried by size. Three flat colour tiles stand in one row, bottom-aligned (align-items: end) with 10px gaps, each larger than the one before: columns 1–3 at 30vh tall, columns 4–7 at 44vh, columns 8–12 at 60vh. Each tile holds one photograph of the subject at that stage (raw, in progress, finished), centred and scaled so the object grows from tile to tile; on light tiles mix-blend-mode: multiply removes a white studio background. One palette colour per tile. Text sits under the tiles, outside them, aligned to each tile's left edge: a stage name at 20px medium whose wording carries the order ('Picked', 'Pressed', 'Poured') and two lines at 16px in the soft ink. The heading, two to four words at 40–52px, occupies the empty ground above the two smaller tiles, top-aligned with the tallest tile. A fourth stage is possible with spans of 2, 3, 3 and 4 columns.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack in order and grow in height instead: 34vw, 46vw and 62vw tall, each at full width. The name and text sit under each tile at 18px and 16px. The heading comes first at 30px. 28px between stages.

sections.name: The itemised receipt
sections.blueprint: For offers made of parts: a base price plus options, a kit, a bundle. A tall paper-coloured slip 380px wide sits in columns 8–11 on a contrasting ground, its bottom edge cut into a zigzag with `clip-path: polygon()`, its top edge running off the top of the section. On the slip, with 28px padding: the name centred at 20px bold, then each item as a row with the description left and the amount right at 16px with tabular figures, 14px between rows; a thick 4px bar in the ink colour; then the total as the largest thing on the slip at 44px, right-aligned. Columns 1–6 carry the heading (two to four words at about 4vw), one paragraph at 18px and the button, starting 96px from the top. If options are selectable, ticking one in the left column adds its row to the slip and updates the total.
sections.mobile: Heading, paragraph and any options come first. The slip follows at 86% width, centred, keeping its zigzag foot, with rows at 16px and the total at 36px. The button sits under the slip at full width, 52px tall.

sections.name: Two-column menu, photo bullets
sections.blueprint: A menu or catalogue list in which each item has a small cut-out photograph where a bullet would be. Each category opens with its name at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 50px) at the left margin and the number of items at 16px right-aligned on the same baseline, with 96px above and 40px below. Items then run in two columns with a 64px gutter and 36px between rows. Each item is a two-part row: a 64px photograph of the item on a plain background at the left (multiplied onto the ground with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, or masked to the page's one shape), then 20px to its right the name in bold at 17–18px with the price right-aligned on the same line, and beneath it a two- or three-line description at 15px in the soft ink, max 38ch. A short note such as an allergen follows the description in the accent ink. No boxes. Holds 6–10 items per category.
sections.mobile: One column. Photographs shrink to 52px and stay at the left; name and price share the first line with the description beneath at 15px. Category names at 8.5vw with the count on the same baseline. A sticky row of category names as text links lets the reader jump.

sections.name: Questions beside a tall photograph
sections.blueprint: One field in a deep or pale flat tone, split 5 to 7. Left, columns 1–5: a heading of two to four words at 36–44px; under it the three or four practical facts people ask first (address, times, how to arrive) as plain lines at 18px; then five or six questions as an accordion with no lines between rows, only 28px of space. Each question is a `<summary>` at 20px with a small chevron drawn from two 2px strokes at its right; the open answer sits beneath at 17px in the softer ink, on the same left edge. One filled button and one text link close the column. Right, columns 7–12: a tall photograph (3:4) that bleeds off the top edge of the section and stops 80px short of the bottom, with a second, square photograph a third of its width overlapping its lower-left corner by 40px.
sections.mobile: The tall photograph leads at full width, 4:5, with the square one overlapping its bottom-right corner at 38% width. Heading at 30px, facts at 17px, then the accordion at full width with 24px between questions and 44px touch targets. Button full width at the end.

sections.name: Name across the last photograph
sections.blueprint: The footer is the page's last photograph, full-bleed at 100vw by 100svh, darkened evenly with `filter: brightness(0.62)` so paper-coloured type reads everywhere on it. Three layers of text sit on the image. Top row, 32px from the edge: a short link list at 16px at the left margin and contact details at the right margin, each no wider than three columns. Mid-height is left to the photograph. Along the bottom, the wordmark runs the full width in the paper colour, letters about 12–20vw tall depending on the name's length, baseline 56px above the edge; under it one line of legal text at 13px. Choose an image whose interest is in its middle band, since the top and bottom carry text. No panel, no box and no colour block separates the footer from the image: the photograph is the footer.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 88svh, cropped to its strongest vertical slice. Links stack at the top-left at 16px, contact beneath them. The wordmark is fitted to the width along the bottom, with the legal line under it at 12px.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.

references.name: starboy
references.idea: A tiny gadget shown enormous: product renders so large the screen crops them, wrapped around a nursery-rhyme headline in fat lowercase.
references.hero: No nav, logo or button. Off-white ground. The right half holds the headline: five stacked lines of very bold rounded lowercase at 13vw (187px), right-aligned and almost touching the right edge, with tight negative tracking and leading under 0.9, so the stack runs from 5% below the top to past the fold and the last line's descenders are cut off. The left 60% is one transparent-shelled, star-shaped device rendered at huge scale (yellow circuit board, round black screen), rotated and cropped by the top, left and bottom edges, its right-hand points tucking behind the letters. A chrome keyring loop peeks in at bottom-right.
references.type: Milling Triplex 1mm, bold, for the headline at 187px in lowercase with -0.055em tracking, one or two words per line over eleven lines; the same family at about 13px for body copy, product names and footer links, all lowercase. Two sizes only, a 14:1 jump.
references.colour: #f9f9f9 #2a2b2d #f5d900 #8d8e96 #b8a45c #2f6fe0 — Off-white page with charcoal type. Colour lives in the objects: circuit-board yellow, chrome, matte black, brass. A small blue logo in the footer is the only interface colour.
references.imagery: Photoreal renders of star-shaped devices in four materials, cut out with no background or cast shadow, scaled well beyond the viewport, each rotated differently and cropped by the edges. Accessories are shown small and centred in grid cells.
references.layout: Three acts: three screens of oversized renders tumbling diagonally with the headline set right, then left; one screen holding a single narrow text column and nothing else; then a three-column hairline-divided product grid running edge to edge with no outer margin.

sections.description: The second and third screens are only renders: a matte-black star and a chrome star overlap on a diagonal, each wider than half the viewport and cropped by two edges. The second half of the headline then appears left-aligned at the same 13vw, left of centre, while a brass star fills the right half and bleeds off the top and right. No captions or interface.

A single column of 13px lowercase text about 290px wide, placed roughly 15% from the left and starting at the top of the viewport: five short paragraphs, the first in medium weight. The remaining three-quarters of the screen is blank off-white. No heading, image or button accompanies it.

Three equal columns span the full viewport width, separated by faint 1px vertical and horizontal lines. Each cell holds one cut-out render centred with generous air and a caption row along its bottom edge: product name at left, price with stock count or a coming-soon note in grey at right, all 13px lowercase. The footer is one row: small blue logo left, five text links right.

steal: Scale the product until two or three viewport edges crop it, and let its silhouette tuck behind the headline letters.
Break a sentence into one or two words per line at 13vw, right-aligned for the first half and left-aligned for the second, so the headline spans several screens.
Follow a loud hero with one tiny text column on an otherwise empty screen; the drop in scale does the pacing.

references.name: Fynza
references.idea: Bookings are drawn as avatar dots whose orange flow lines merge into a single vertical spine, which then runs down the page as the axis for the partner list, the cash-flow timeline and the step cards.
references.hero: Warm grey ground with a fine white dot texture and a peach gradient bleeding down from the top edge. A floating white pill navbar 80% wide holds the logo left and a language switch plus outlined and orange pill buttons right. Centred stack: a white pill badge with overlapping partner-logo dots, a two-line extra-bold uppercase headline at 4.2vw in slate navy with two words in orange, two lines of grey 18px text, an orange pill button. Around the button five round avatar photos with small booking labels sit at staggered heights across the full width; thin orange curves, two dashed, flow down from each and converge at bottom centre.
references.type: Golos Text only: weight 800 uppercase at 60px for every section headline with slight negative tracking, 18px regular grey body, about 24px semibold for card titles, tiny uppercase captions. A wide extended logo wordmark. Roughly four sizes; hierarchy relies on weight and colour.
references.colour: #edecea #ffffff #f4bba8 #f2561d #3f4f6e #1a2e7a — Warm grey and white with peach gradients fading in at section tops and bottoms; orange carries buttons, flow lines and highlighted headline words; one deep royal-navy slab near the end.
references.imagery: Round avatar photos, partner logo discs, sunny travel photographs inside rounded cards with white UI snippets floating on top, and illustrated vintage postage stamps tilted and scattered around the final call to action.
references.layout: Centred container of about 1150px; every section opens with a small white pill label and a two-line uppercase headline. A single orange vertical line runs through the page centre linking hero, logo list, timeline and step cards. Sections alternate grey, peach fade and one navy slab.

sections.description: Directly under the hero the converged orange line becomes a vertical spine and partner brands hang off it in two columns: logo then name on the left, name then logo on the right. Rows are separated by dashed horizontal rules with small orange dots where they cross the spine. There is no heading, so it reads as a continuation of the hero diagram.

Problem timeline on the centre spine: small rounded-square chips labelled by week sit on the line. Events alternate left and right, each joined to its chip by a dashed horizontal line ending in a small coloured amount tag (red for outflow, green for income), with a bold label and two lines of grey text. A red-tinted rounded note sits on the spine as the conclusion while the background fades to saturated peach.

Three large white rounded cards stacked on the spine, each a two-column split that alternates sides: on one side an orange numbered disc, a three-line semibold title and a small grey paragraph; on the other a rounded travel photograph with a white UI card or a cluster of logo discs floating over it. The orange line passes behind the gaps between cards.

Dotted peach-to-white field with a centred two-line uppercase headline, one word in orange, and an orange pill button. Six illustrated vintage travel stamps and round stickers are scattered around it at slight rotations, three above and three below, some tucked under the navbar. A tiny two-line legal footer sits directly underneath, centred, with no separate footer band.

steal: Turn the hero illustration's lines into a page-long spine: let the curves converge at the fold and continue as the axis for the next section's list and timeline.
Show the customer's own unit of value (a booking with name, party size and price) as small avatar chips instead of a dashboard screenshot.
End on a themed sticker scatter (illustrated stamps at varied tilt) around the last call to action rather than a plain coloured band.
